items.title: Wine 11.23 Released With Support For ARM64 macOS, AVX In 32-bit Emulation On ARM64
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>We are getting close to the Wine 12.0 release candidate phase but out today is Wine 11.23 as the latest bi-weekly development release continuing to land new features into Wine...</article>

items.title: GMKtec EVO-X2 AMD Ryzen AI Max+ Strix Halo Mini PC
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>For those in the market for an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ mini PC but not able to procure the likes of the Ryzen AI Halo or Framework Desktop in your region or with elevated pricing, another Strix Halo option that's been available is the GMKtec EVO-X2. I recently received a review sample of the GMKtec EVO-X2 and put it through a variety of benchmarks in seeing how the performance stacks up against the flagship Ryzen AI Halo and Framework Desktop offerings as well as the BOSGAME VTA-439 powered by the AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 for reference plus also the Dell Pro Max GB10 powered by the NVIDIA GB10 SoC.</article>

items.title: New "Earthqaic" Gallium3D Driver Merged For Mesa 27.0
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Merged today to Mesa Git is a brand new Gallium3D driver: Earthqaic...</article>

items.title: Linux Dropping Last Of The 1980's VersaModular Eurocard "VME" vme_user Code Over AI/LLM Noise
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The Linux kernel is removing more old driver code due to AI/LLMs generating more noise over this unused, obsolete code within the source tree. Following various old ISA and PCMCIA code removed, ham radio, ISDN, and other old network code, the latest vintage artifact set to be stripped out of the Linux kernel is around the VersaModular Eurocard "VME" bus vme_user driver from the 1980s...</article>

items.title: Linux Mint 27 Beta Released With New Apps, Full Wayland Support
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Ahead of the official release expected around Christmas, the beta of Linux Mint 27 was announced today for testing...</article>

items.title: systemd 263-rc1 Ships Initial Rust Code, Experimental Pseudo TTY Broker & Manifest
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Systemd 263-rc1 was just tagged in gearing up for this next major release. Systemd 263 brings initial support for using the Rust programming language for creating new Rust programs. Plus systemd 263 ships with a new pseudo TTY broker service, a manifest tool, a new keyring service and much more...</article>

items.title: Intel's Vulkan Linux Driver Now Enables Efficient 64-bit Mode "e64" By Default
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Debuting with the upcoming Intel Nova Lake P processors with their Xe3P integrated graphics is a new efficient 64-bit addressing mode "e64". This efficient 64-bit addressing mode for the future Intel GPUs provides native 64-bit shader memory addressing as a replacement to the 32-bit offset mode used by Intel GPU shaders up to now. As of the latest Mesa Git code, the Intel ANV Vulkan driver is enabling the e64 mode by default...</article>

items.title: ZenSMU Provides A Rust CLI/TUI & GUI For AMD Ryzen Monitoring/Tweaking
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>In the absence of any official AMD Ryzen Master utility for Linux to extensively monitor your Ryzen processor and overclocking/tweaking the CPU, there are a few unofficial, open-source utilities out there that aim for a similar intent. One of the new ones is ZenSMU that provides both a CLI/TUI interface and a proper Linux desktop GUI...</article>

items.title: Intel Compute Runtime 26.44.40734.8 Had OpenCL 3.1 But Reverted, More Performance
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Intel on Thursday released their Compute Runtime 26.44.40734.8 release as the latest feature update to this open-source GPU compute stack used on Linux and Windows...</article>

items.title: Reminder: Black Friday Deal & The Unfortunate Ad Network Situation This Year
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>To all Phoronix readers a happy holidays. Just a friendly reminder about the ongoing "Black Friday" special at Phoronix to help support the site after a particularly struggling year while continuing to provide daily Linux hardware reviews and open-source news...</article>

items.title: Initial AMD RDNA5 Support To Appear In Linux 7.5
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Earlier this month the initial AMD GFX13 / GC 13 IP patches were posted for that next-generation graphics IP block expected to be for the RDNA5 graphics processors. With coincidental timing, that initial RDNA5 graphics driver enablement work is now on track for landing in the Linux 7.5 kernel...</article>

items.title: Omarchy 4.6-RC1 Released With More Local AI Integration, Its Own File Manager
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The Arch Linux based Omarchy distribution that continues seeing the backing of notable industry players is out with a new release. Omarchy 4.6 continues the project's quest of being a very AI forward Linux distribution and continuing to evolve more from its original Arch Linux and Hyprland customizations...</article>

items.title: It Looks Like AI Agent Skills Will Be Submitted For Linux 7.5
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>For the upcoming Linux 7.5 merge window happening in late December, it appears that AI agent skills will be submitted for adding in-tree documentation for instructing AI agents on different kernel processes...</article>

items.title: Amid All The AI Generated Patches & Bug Reports, Linux Gains Another Network Maintainer
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Linux networking developers have previously said they've been "completely overwhelmed" with all the AI/LLM-driven activity from bug reports to patches over the past year. In an increasing number of cases, they end up diverting fixes to the next Linux kernel version due to the seemingly endless activity. All the AI activity around seldom used drivers and other networking areas also led to removing various old networking code. As some good news, another Linux developer has now been promoted to being an additional Linux networking subsystem maintainer...</article>

items.title: Ubuntu 27.04 Snapshot 1 Released For Testing
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>For those with extra time around the US Thanksgiving holiday, the first Tenacious Snapshot 1 was just released today as the first stepping stone toward Ubuntu 27.04...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.4 Delivers Some Performance Gains For Intel Panther Lake's Arc B390 Graphics
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With the recently reviewed Dell XPS 14 laptop powered by Intel Core Ultra Series 3 "Panther Lake", it ships with Ubuntu 26.04 LTS as one of the Dell supported options. If aiming for maximizing the performance out of Panther Lake, upgrading to Ubuntu 26.10 provides some performance boosts. If wanting to take things even further, going with the in-development Linux 7.4 kernel provides some advantages particularly for the Arc B390 integrated Xe3 graphics...</article>

items.title: DXVK 3.2 Released With Present Timing Support
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>DXVK 3.2 is out today as the newest feature release for this Vulkan-based implementation of the Direct3D 8 through Direct3D 11 APIs that is used by Valve's Steam Play (Proton)...</article>

items.title: Brush 0.5 Passing 96+% Of Upstream Test Suite For Bash Shell Written In Rust
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Brush as the open-source project providing a Bash/POSIX-compatible shell written in Rust is out with its newest feature release. With Brush 0.5 they are passing over 96% of the upstream bash-completion test suite thanks to a variety of improvements made this release cycle. Most Bash scripts should be able to run unchanged under Brush...</article>

items.title: F2FS Getting Ready With Its Large Folios Support
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>In recent months there has been a lot of work done by developer Nanzhe Zhao on implementing support for large folios for most readable/writable files with the F2FS file-system in its buffered I/O paths. This can bring some performance benefits and it's looking like the work may be wrapped up in time for the Linux 7.5 kernel...</article>

items.title: Intel Xe Driver Gaining PCIe Function Level Reset "FLR" With Linux 7.5
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Last week's drm-xe-next pull request of new Xe kernel driver material that Intel has ready for Linux 7.5 finally introduces PCIe Function Level Reset (FLR) support for this modern Intel graphics driver...</article>

items.title: KosmicKrisp Now The Go-To Solution For Vulkan On Macs In Place Of MoltenVK
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>While MoltenVK began as an initiative to layer the Vulkan API atop Apple's Metal for use on macOS and iOS, the KosmicKrisp effort spearheaded by LunarG is now the go-to solution for Vulkan API support on modern Apple devices...</article>

items.title: PostgreSQL 19 Delivering Nice Performance Gains, Benchmarks On 6th Gen AMD EPYC Venice
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Last week PostgreSQL 19.0 finally shipped after being delayed due to the AI/LLM burden facing open-source developers this year. The wait is worth it though as PostgreSQL 19 is showing some very nice performance gains over PostgreSQL 18 in my benchmarking. Here are some initial PostgreSQL 19 vs. 18 database server benchmarks on the new 6th Gen AMD EPYC Venice platform.</article>

items.title: Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS vs. Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS Benchmarks
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>System76 released Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS yesterday as the newest version of their Ubuntu-derived Linux distribution featuring their in-house COSMIC desktop environment. For those curious about any performance differences out of Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS, I already have some benchmarks comparing it to the former 24.04 release since the new System76 Thelio Prime SFF PC has been shipping with 26.04 LTS since last week.</article>

items.title: Servo Now Supports HTML Video Captions, Flutter Web Content Working
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The Rust-based Servo open-source web browser engine and Servoshell demo browser enjoyed a lot of new features in October. Servo 0.8 debuted recently with all of their October changes and out today is a blog post to highlight their latest round of improvements...</article>

items.title: GNU Linux-Libre Celebrates Reverse Engineered Firmware For Old 802.11 b/g WiFi Chipset
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Coming as a surprise today was a new GNU Linux-libre kernel release for the older Linux 6.12 LTS kernel. Typically it's uncommon seeing new updates for old/LTS kernels announced by the project, but today they are celebrating a WiFi chipset now working with their sanitized version of the Linux kernel. If you don't mind using legacy 802.11 b/g WiFi, there is a newly endorsed driver option...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.5 Whitelisting Intel Xeon Server CPUs For Peer-To-Peer DMA "P2PDMA"
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>For those making use of VMware virtualization or other scenarios, the upcoming Linux 7.5 kernel will see that peer-to-peer DMA "P2PDMA" is properly enabled for modern Intel Xeon servers. This follows a similar change already in place for AMD Zen-based platforms to ensure P2PDMA usage is properly whitelisted...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.4 Disables LLVM Profi Usage To Avoid Performance Hit, Pathological Build Times
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>A change merged this week to the Linux 7.4 kernel and also set to be back-ported to stable kernel branches is to disable use of LLVM's Profi flow-based profile inference algorithm when leveraging AutoFDO...</article>

items.title: 3mdeb Updates Their Open-Source Coreboot-Based Firmware For MSI PRO Z690-A/Z790-P
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Four years ago the 3mdeb firmware consulting firm managed an incredible feat in bringing Coreboot to a modern, retail desktop motherboard with the current Intel Core processors of the time. This was a port of their Coreboot-powered Dasharo firmware to the MSI PRO Z690-A motherboard and then to the newer MSI PRO Z790-P motherboard. Today they released updated firmware builds for those still making use of the Intel Alder Lake and Raptor Lake era hardware...</article>

items.title: Alien Arena Comes To Flathub, Rolls Out Many Optimizations
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>It's been a long while since hearing anything new out of Alien Arena, the open-source first person shooter game that is based on a sci-fi theme with a Quake II/III derived engine, but it's still alive and kicking. This week it also made its latest update on Flathub to become even more accessible to Linux gamers...</article>

items.title: Benchmarking The Performance Benefit Of FRED On AMD Zen 6
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With the new EPYC 9006 SP7 Venice processors now shipping, one of the curious follow-up benchmarks I have been wanting to pursue is around quantifying the performance impact of Flexible Return and Event Delivery "FRED". After all, FRED showed very nice gains for Intel Panther Lake for first featuring FRED. Since then the Linux kernel has enabled FRED usage by default with capable CPUs, so all the EPYC 9006 benchmarks on Phoronix have already been with FRED, so here are some numbers when going ahead and forcing FRED off in the Linux kernel...</article>

items.title: Linus Torvalds: "Tell Your AI Companion To Get Its Act Together"
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>A big EXT4 pull request today intended for the Linux 7.4-rc5 kernel has set off Linus Torvalds. Over 41k lines of new code in this EXT4 pull request going in as "fixes".... Much of that being new KUnit test coverage to make it safer to validate AI-generated patches. And then a lot of AI generated patches themselves for the EXT4 file-system...</article>

items.title: Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS Released With More COSMIC Apps, Remote Desktop & More
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>System76 has a wonderful surprise today with the release of Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS as the newest iteration of their in-house Linux distribution now built atop the Ubuntu 26.04 LTS package base and incorporating their latest enhancements to their COSMIC desktop...</article>
